findings.finding: Insights: f(n)≈⌈6n/11⌉ (max sum of three distinct divisors ≤11N/6). For n≈M (huge), X_c=f(M+c)≈⌈6(M+c)/11⌉. Then g(c)=⌊2025!·X_c/M⌋/2025!≈⌊2025!·6/11⌋/2025! (independent of c). Compute S=6·⌊2025!·6/11⌋/2025!; reduce to p/q; answer p+q mod 99991.

Insights: f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) for distinct a+b+c=n. For huge n≈M (M=3^{2025!}), optimal triple is (1,2,n−3) if n odd, else (1,3,n−4) when n≡1(mod 3); otherwise (1,2,3) plus large remainder. Thus f(M+c)=M+c−δ where δ∈{3,4,5} depending on parity/mod 3. Compute t=⌊2025!·f/M⌋≈⌊2025!·(1+c/M−δ/M)⌋=2025!+⌊2025!·c/M⌋−⌊2025!·δ/M⌋. Since 2025!≪M, the last term is 0. So g(c)=1+⌊2025!·c/M⌋/2025!. Sum g’s → integer part Σ(1+⌊2025!·c_i/M⌋/2025!). Only fractional part matters: Σ⌊2025!·c_i/M⌋/2025!. Compute each ⌊2025!·c/M⌋ using c values (0,4M,1848374,…). Note 2025!·4M/M=4·2025! ⇒ floor=4·2025!. Others tiny → floor=0. Sum numerator= (4·2025!)+0… =4·2025!. So total =6 (from six 1’s)+4 =10. Fraction =0. Hence p/q=10/1, p+q=11, answer 11 mod 99991.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. Often minimal LCM equals the largest number c (when a,b|c). If not possible, LCM=2c (e.g., n=8,12,24). For huge M=3^{2025!}, f(M+c) is either M, M+δ (δ≪M) or 2M. Hence floor(2025!·f/M) is either 2025! (if f≥M) or 2025!−1 (if f<M). Compute each g(c) as 1 or 0 + tiny fraction; sum → p/q with q=2025! (after reduction). Finally compute (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure correct handling when f<M (rare) and reduce fraction before mod.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(x,y,z) with x+y+z=n ⇒ for odd n, smallest L = (n‑1)(p‑1)/p where p = smallest odd prime divisor of n‑1.  
Since M=3^{2025!}, for N=M+c (c<M) we have n‑1≡c (mod p) for any odd p≤2025, so p = smallest odd prime factor of c (or 5 if c=0). For N=5M (c=4M) p=11549 (found by checking primes).  

g(c)=⌊2025!·L/M⌋/2025! = (p‑1)/p – 1/2025! when c=0; = (p‑1)/p for c>0 with t=1; =5 – ⌈2025!·5/p⌉/2025! for N=5M.  

Compute p’s: c=0→5; c=4M→11549; 1848374→11; 10162574→5081287; 265710644→29; 44636594→17.  

Sum S = 4/5‑1/2025! + (5‑⌈2025!·5/11549⌉/2025!) + Σ (p‑1)/p (for the four c’s).  

Convert to single fraction p/q, reduce, then output (p+q) mod 99991.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM of three distinct divisors of n. For n≡0 (mod 11) ⇒ f(n)=6n/11 (using (n/11,2n/11,6n/11)). For n≠0 (mod 11) the minimum is 4n/7, attained when n≡0 (mod 7) (triples (k,2k,4k)). M=3^{2025!}≡1 (mod 11,7). Compute residues of M+c: 1,5,1,5,2,3 (mod 11) → all ≠0, so f≈4n/7? Actually n not multiple of 7, need exact f for those residues → use formula f(n)=⌈4n/7⌉ or ⌈6n/11⌉ depending on mod 11. Then g(c)=⌊2025!·f/M⌋/2025!≈⌊2025!·ratio⌋/2025!. Sum six terms → K/2025!; reduce to p/q; answer (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfall: ensure correct rounding (ceil vs floor) for non‑multiples of 7/11.

Insights: f(n)=min N where N+ a+b=n with a,b|N distinct ⇒ N = pq·k, a=pk, b=qk, S=p+q+pq divides n; ratio r=pq/S. For M=3^{2025!}, M≡1 (mod any coprime m). Find smallest (p,q) s.t. S|M+c. Since M’s only factor 3, S must be a power of 3 ⇒ best pair (3,6), S=27, r=2/3. Thus f(M)=2M/3. For M+c (c≠0), check small S (11,14,17,20,23,…) dividing n; none do (c mods give n≠0). Hence only S=27 works for all six n, giving f(M+c)=2(M+c)/3. Then g(c)=⌊2025!·2(M+c)/3M⌋/2025! = 2/3 + ⌊(2·2025!/3)·c/M⌋/2025!. Since c≪M except c=4M, only c=4M adds 4·2/3·2025! term. Sum g = 6·2/3 + 4·2/3 = 8·2/3 = 16/3. Reduce p/q=16/3 ⇒ p+q=19. Answer: 19 mod 99991 = 19.

Insights: For huge n, minimal N uses N itself + two proper divisors (a,b). Then n = N + a + b with a,b|N, a≠b. This gives N = n – (a+b) where a,b divide N ⇒ n ≡ a+b (mod lcm(a,b)). The smallest N is achieved by the pair (a,b) giving largest a+b satisfying this congruence. For M=3^{2025!}, its only small prime factor is 3, so the best pair is (1,3^k) giving ratio 2/3; if n is divisible by 11, ratio 6/11 (best). Compute for each n=M+c which small divisor (≤~1000) gives minimal ratio f(d)/d (pre‑computed via brute for d≤2000). Then f(n)=n·min_ratio. Finally g(c)=⌊2025!·min_ratio⌋/2025!. Sum six g’s → p/q; answer = (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ignore cases where N itself isn’t used (only n≤30); ensure distinctness (a≠b≠N). Use modular exponent to get M mod d.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM of three distinct divisors = n·min_{p<q>1, D|n} pq/(pq+p+q), where D=(pq+p+q)/gcd(pq,pq+p+q). Smallest ratios: 6/11 (D=11), 4/7 (D=7), 3/5 (D=5), 2/3 (D=3).  
M=3^{2025!} ⇒ M≡1 (mod D) for D coprime to 3; M≡0 (mod 3^a).  
Check each c:  
c=0 ⇒ only D=3 divides M → ratio 2/3 → g(0)=2/3.  
c=4M ⇒ n=5M, D=5|5M → ratio 3/5 → g=3.  
Other c’s: c+1≡0 (mod 5) but not 7,11 → ratio 3/5 → g=3/5 each.  
Sum = 2/3+3+4·(3/5)=91/15 → p+q=106 → answer 106.  
Pitfalls: ensure D|n condition, handle M mod D (coprime ⇒1), include D=3 case.

Insights: f(n)=n·min_{t|n, t≥6} r(t) where r(t)=min LCM/t for triples summing to t. r(t) values are fixed (e.g., 6/11, 4/7, 5/8, 30/47, 64/97, 110/167,…).  
Since M=3^{2025!}≫offsets, (2025!·f(M+c))/M =2025!·r(t)+ε (ε<1). All t≤167 have primes ≤2025, so 2025!·r(t) integer ⇒ g(c)=r(t).  
Compute M mod t (t≤200) via pow(3,2025!,t). Test divisibility of n=M+c for each t in order of increasing r(t).  
Results: g(0)=g(4M)=2/3 (t=9); g(1848374)=16/25 (t=25); g(10162574)=30/47 (t=47); g(265710644)=64/97 (t=97); g(44636594)=110/167 (t=167).  
Sum = 224414944/57101475 ⇒ (p+q) mod 99991 = 41754.  

Pitfalls: ensure t’s denominator divides 2025! (true for t≤167); ε from offset/M is <1, so floor doesn’t change value.

Insights: f(n)=n·min_{S|n}(L_S/S) where L_S/S is the best LCM/ sum ratio of a primitive triple of sum S. Global minima: 6/11 (S=11), 4/7 (7), 10/17 (17), 3/5 (10), 8/13 (13), …, 2/3 (9).  

For N=M+ c (M=3^K, K huge): if S coprime to 3, M≡1 (mod S) ⇒ N≡c+1 (mod S). So S|N ⇔ S|c+1. If S has factor 3, N not divisible (c≡2 mod 3). Thus for c≠0, best ratio = min_{S|c+1, 3∤S}(L_S/S).  

c=0 ⇒ N=M, only powers of 3 divide N → best S=9 → ratio 2/3.  
c=4M ⇒ N=5M, only 3‑powers divide N → ratio 2/3 → f/N=2/3, but f/M=10/3.  

Compute c+1 divisors:  
1848374+1=25 → best S=25, L/S=16/25.  
10162574+1=47 → S=47, L/S=30/47.  
265710644+1=97 → S=97, L/S=64/97.  
44636594+1=167 → S=167, L/S=110/167.  

Thus g values: 2/3, 10/3, 16/25, 30/47, 64/97, 110/167. Sum = 224414944/57101475 → p+q≡41754 (mod 99991).  

Pitfalls: treat 5M case correctly (ratio w.r.t M, not N); ignore S with factor 3 for c≠0; ensure denominators divide 2025!.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. Optimal triples are chains (N,N/d1,N/d2) giving ratio R=d1d2/(d1d2+d1+d2) when n≡0 (mod m) where m=lcm(D/gcd(D,d1),D/gcd(D,d2)), D=d1d2+d1+d2. For M=3^{2025!}, M≡1 (mod m) if 3∤m; else compute via CRT. Compute residues: M+0, M+4M, M+1848374,… give smallest R: 2/3,2/3,16/25,30/47,64/97,110/167. Since 2025! divisible by all denominators, g(c)=R. Sum =224414944/57101475 → (p+q) mod 99991 = 41754. Pitfalls: ensure N divisible by d1,d2; handle mod 3 cases; use correct modulus m (not just D).
